panels.figure_caption: A 3D CT image of a sagittal CRS (scaphocephaly) with an elongated skull, a prominent forehead, and occipital bulging. The white arrow indicates an abnormally fused suture.
in_text_mentions: Sagittal CRS is the most common form of nonsyndromic CRS. It involves the premature fusion of the sagittal suture, which runs from the front to the back of the skull. This fusion restricts the lateral growth of the skull, resulting in a long, narrow head shape known as scaphocephaly (or dolichocephaly) (Figure 2).

in_text_mentions: Metopic CRS involves the premature fusion of the metopic suture, which runs from the top of the head down the middle of the forehead to the nose. This leads to a triangular forehead, a condition also known as trigonocephaly (Figure 5).

panels.figure_caption: A 3D CT image of complex nonsyndromic CRS in a 6-month-old patient diagnosed with skull deformity. (A) Right frontal eminence asymmetry (white arrow) and minor left posterior plagiocephaly, with incipient sagittal synostosis (yellow arrow) and the presence of a right parietal accessory suture (red arrow). Subsequent 1-year follow-up examination (B) confirmed mild skull deformity due to complete fusion of the sagittal suture, not resulting in classic scaphocephaly due to patency of the PA suture.
in_text_mentions: Some cases involve the premature fusion of multiple major or minor sutures, leading to complex cranial shapes and increased ICP. These cases can present with a combination of features from different types of craniosynostoses and, occasionally, can be nonsyndromic (Figure 7). Genetic mutations are major determining factors in complex craniosynostoses [19].

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (a, b, C). a: Sagittal 2D CT in trigonocephaly surgical cohort for metopic angle measurement; in-text defines angle at most protruding point of metopic ridge, supporting metopic ridge / trigonocephaly manifestation. b: Coronal 2D CT in same trigonocephaly measurement set; supraorbital plane measurement for metopic ridge assessment in disease-focused article on trigonocephaly patients. C: Axial supraorbital CT shows pointed triangular forehead / keel-shaped anterior contour with angle arms on frontal bone, visually showing trigonocephaly in metopic synostosis case from trigonocephaly article.
panels.attribution_text: Baş and Baş. Craniometric Measurements and Surgical Outcomes in Trigonocephaly Patients Who Underwent Surgical Treatment.. Cureus 2021. doi:10.7759/cureus.13676. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Metopic angle measurements in the supraorbital plane a: sagittal; b: coronal; c: axial
in_text_mentions: MA angle measurements in the supraorbital plane are presented below (Figure 1). MA is defined as follows: in supraorbital 2D axial CT sections, the angle in the axial section parallel to the orbital ceiling, the corner of which is at the most protruding point of the metopic ridge and the arms extending laterally on the frontal bone surface [5,6].
